candidates.spoken: Humanity's deepest hole stopped at 12,262 metres.
What If We Tried to Drill Through the Earth?
The drill fails in the crust.
Heat stopped them: 180 °C, far above what they expected.
They aimed for 15,000 metres and fell short.
Engineers tried to drill toward Earth's centre.
Drilling at Kola SG-3 began in 1970 using the Uralmash-4E.
So the planet's first defence against drilling is heat, not hardness.
Soviet engineers began drilling Kola SG-3 in 1970.
Deeper down, the heat and pressure only climb.
It would not all happen at once.
The real cause was temperature and pressure rise with depth.
Rock that hot starts behaving more like plastic than stone.
A total of five 23-centimetre-diameter (9 in) boreholes were drilled.
The third hole reached 12,262 metres (40,230 ft) in 1989.
Temperature and pressure rise with depth, softening rock and destroying drilling equipment.

script.spoken: Humanity's deepest hole stopped at 12,262 metres. It barely scratched the crust. Soviet engineers began drilling Kola SG-3 in 1970. They aimed for 15,000 metres and fell short. Heat stopped them: 180 °C, far above what they expected. Rock that hot starts behaving more like plastic than stone. Deeper down, the heat and pressure only climb. So the planet's first defence against drilling is heat, not hardness.
